title: Together Link: open models in the harness you already use. Start with one command today.
gist: Together AI launches Together Link, a one-command shim that points existing coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode etc.) at open models on its serverless platform, claiming over 50% spend cuts. It routes per session between frontier and cheap models and cites its share of OpenRouter token volume for several open models.

themes.theme: Open models as cost arbitrage for coding agents

insights.claim: Together AI claims that routing coding-agent workloads to open models through Together Link cuts customer spend by over 50% with the same agent and workflow.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Vendor-claimed savings signal pricing pressure on premium closed coding models.

insights.claim: Engineering orgs are said to spend tens of thousands to millions of dollars a month on closed models because every task, from one-line fixes to full rewrites, often runs on the same premium model.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Undifferentiated model use is the waste being targeted; coding-agent spend is a large budget line.

insights.claim: Open models such as Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 are claimed to handle many of the hardest coding tasks at a fraction of closed per-token prices, while Flash-class models (GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) cover everyday coding.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: The open-versus-closed quality gap is narrowing enough to erode closed-lab pricing power in coding.
insights.locator: Open models have meaningfully closed the gap

insights.claim: A per-session tracker compares actual spend with what the same session would have cost on Opus 5.5, turning savings into a visible, sticky metric for buyers.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Benchmarking against the closed flagship makes the cost gap legible to engineering managers.
insights.locator: See your savings after each session

insights.claim: Together Link works inside existing harnesses (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex in ChatGPT app and CLI, OpenCode, Pi), keeping settings and logins, with a one-command revert to native closed models, which minimizes switching cost.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: The harness layer is being commoditized; closed labs' own agent front-ends can be used as a distribution channel for rival models.

insights.claim: The Auto router reads each session's first task and sends quick fixes to fast low-cost models and hard problems to frontier capability; with an Anthropic key it routes between Opus 5.5 and GLM 5.3, without one between GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Hybrid routing positions open models as a complement to closed ones, not only a replacement.

insights.claim: Routing happens once per session rather than per message so that prompt caching keeps working, an explicit tradeoff of routing granularity for cache economics.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Prompt-cache hit rates constrain how finely agent workloads can be split across models.

insights.claim: Billing uses the customer's existing Together API key on serverless pay-as-you-go or credit packs with no separate contract, lowering procurement friction.
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Bottom-up developer adoption can bypass enterprise procurement for inference vendors.

insights.claim: As of 9/30/2026, Together AI serves the largest share of OpenRouter tokens for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (40.8%), GLM 5.3 Flash (28.2%) and Kimi K3 (23.1%).
insights.speaker: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
insights.so_what: Shows Together is a leading host of Chinese open models, though shares are far from dominant and self-reported.

source_meta.author: Will Van Eaton, Hassan El Mghari
